This entry uses the corrected dates and periods from KFF and the Congressional Research Service. It replaces the inaccurate claim that retroactive coverage ended completely and distinguishes the renewal requirement from the separate limit on retroactive coverage.

frozen_original.title: Trump Administration Defies Court Orders on Deportation Flights
frozen_original.synopsis: On March 15, 2025, the Trump administration proceeded with deportation flights of Venezuelan nationals under the Alien Enemies Act in direct defiance of U.S. District Judge James Boasberg's temporary restraining order, which had explicitly prohibited such flights while the court considered the matter. The case raised a direct conflict between executive control of deportation operations and judicial authority to preserve the court’s ability to review removals. The judge’s finding and the administration’s legal position remained competing parts of the case; the appellate process continued after the contempt inquiry began. The episode put the timing and handling of the flights at the center of a consequential dispute over due process and the limits of presidential power.

Trump's characterizations were consistently applied to cities with large Black populations — Detroit, Chicago, Baltimore — and used as a backdrop for immigration policy attacks, falsely implying immigrants were causing the violence. Civil rights organizations and Black elected officials condemned the rhetoric as a dehumanizing caricature that ignored actual crime trends and community investment. The characterizations were part of a broader campaign strategy to appeal to white grievance while simultaneously claiming to be a champion for Black Americans.
